card.statement:
We offer two extremal examples of elements of $\operatorname{Q}_{\mathcal{N},\Gamma}(Z(\mathfrak{g}))$ when $\Gamma$ is the trivial group. The enveloping algebra gives rise to an element $(\mathrm{U}(\mathfrak{g}),Z(\mathfrak{g}),i)$. On the other hand, one can take $\mathrm{U}(\mathfrak{g})/(\ker\chi_{0})\otimes_{\mathbb{C}}Z(\mathfrak{g})$ where $\chi_{0}:Z(\mathfrak{g})\to\mathbb{C}$ is the character of the trivial representation. The former is the largest quantization of $\mathcal{N}$, in a sense which we make precise in the following section. The latter is a quantization of the trivial deformation of $\mathcal{N}$.

13.4. Universal elements of the deformation and quantization functors

We recap the basics of universal elements of functors, see [Ma71, III.1] for more detail. Let ${\mathbf{C}}$ be a category. A functor $\mathcal{F}:\mathbf{C}\to\mathbf{Set}$ is representable over a base $B$ if there exists a natural equivalence $\mathrm{Hom}_{\textbf{C}}(B,\cdot)\to\mathcal{F}$, and a representation of $\mathcal{F}$ is a choice of natural equivalence, and $B$ may be called the base of the representation.

A universal element of $\mathcal{F}$ is a pair $(B,b)$ with $b\in\mathcal{F}(B)$ such that for every other such pair $(C,c)$ there exists a unique $\phi\in\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{C}}(B,C)$ such that $\mathcal{F}(\phi)(b)=c$. By Yoneda’s lemma, every representable functor admits a universal element: if $\mathcal{F}$ is represented by $B$ then $b\in\mathcal{F}(\operatorname{Id}_{B})(B)$ supplies a universal element. If the base $B$ is clear, then we often just write $b$ for the universal element. Note that the choice of universal element is not unique. Every automorphism $\phi\in\mathrm{Aut}_{\mathbf{C}}(B)$ gives rise to a universal element, and so the set of universal elements of $\mathcal{F}$ is an $\mathrm{Aut}_{\mathbf{C}}(B)$ -torsor.

Namikawa has shown that for a conic symplectic singularity $X$ the functor of (formal) Poisson deformations is prorepresentable and unobstructed [Na11], and in the sequel [Na10] he used the conic structure to show that the functor $\operatorname{PD}_{X}$ is representable (see [ACET23] for a algebraic survey of these results). If $B_{X}\in\textbf{GrAlg}$ represents $\operatorname{PD}_{X}$ then an element of $\operatorname{PD}_{X}(B_{X})$ is called a universal Poisson deformation of $\mathbb{C}[X]$ (we drop the words flat graded for brevity), and the group of graded automorphisms of $B_{X}$ acts simply transitively on $\operatorname{PD}_{X}(B_{X})$ (this algebra was denoted $B_{u}$ in [ACET23]).

Losev proved in [Lo22, Prop. 3.5] that Namikawa’s universal flat graded Poisson deformation of $\mathbb{C}[X]$ admits a filtered quantization which satisfies a certain universal property. In [ACET23, §2.7&2.8] this universal property was reformulated in terms of the functor $\operatorname{Q}_{X}$, and upgraded to the $\Gamma$ -equivariant setting.

paper.title: Shifted twisted Yangians and finite $W$-algebras of classical type
paper.abstract: We introduce parabolic presentations of twisted Yangians of types AI and AII, interpolating between the R-matrix presentation and the Drinfeld presentation. Then we formulate and provide parabolic presentations for the shifted twisted Yangians. We define quotient algebras known as truncated shifted twisted Yangians and equip them with baby comultiplications, generalizing the work of Brundan and Kleshchev. PBW bases for all (truncated) shifted twisted Yangians of type AI and AII are established along the way. Applying the theory of universal equivariant quantizations of conic symplectic singularities we show that the truncated twisted shifted Yangian is isomorphic to the finite $W$-algebra which quantizes a suitable Slodowy slice. This provides a presentation of the finite $W$-algebra associated with every even nilpotent element in type {\sf B} and {\sf C}, as well as every nilpotent element with two Jordan blocks in type {\sf D}. Finally we make a conjecture which would supply presentations in the remaining even cases in type {\sf D}.
